title: What is known about 1RB0LD_0RC---_0LD0RF_1LE1LD_0LA0RD_0RB1RA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LD_0RC---_0LD0RF_1LE1LD_0LA0RD_0RB1RA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state machine halts from blank tape. Seen from the left end, its tape is mostly two long runs of the word 100 / 1100 with a marker between them; seen from the right end, it is one long run of 1100 with about as many words, after a short disordered stretch. Its near-twin 1RB0LF_1LC0RD_1LA1LC_---0RE_0RB1RA_1LC1LF does the same.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 107 steps; the C simulator shows none in 109. How the disordered stretch evolves is not yet understood.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (B1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 2,925 cells have been visited and 1,451 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Tape shape
claims.text: At the last side switches before 109 steps the tape is, at the left end, 0 0 0 (100)^6 1100 (100)^4 (1100)^398 1 (1100)^319 100 (1100)^2 0 1100 (step 998,319,040); at the right end, … (1100)^717 1 1100 0 0 0 (1100)^3 after a disordered stretch of 37 cells (step 999,616,144). The two runs at the left (409 + 308, then 398 + 319) add up to the one run at the right (716, then 717), to within one word.

claims.title: A twin
claims.text: 1RB0LD_0RC---_0LD0RF_1LE1LD_0LA0RD_0RB1RA and 1RB0LF_1LC0RD_1LA1LC_---0RE_0RB1RA_1LC1LF behave alike: all 1,423 side switches in the first 109 steps fall on the same sides in both, the widths at the n-th switch differ by at most 1, and the run lengths printed agree (409 and 308, 398 and 319, 716, 717).

claims.title: Growth shape: power/power
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.324). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.328).

claims.title: Growth like t<sup>1/3</sup>
claims.text: After step 5·10<sup>8</sup>: 298 side switches, 1,676,606 steps apart on average (≈ 0.196·w<sup>2</sup>, w = 2924), about 2.0 cells of width per switch; fitted width exponent 0.326 after step 10<sup>7</sup>.

claims.title: How it could halt
claims.text: The halting transition is B reading 1. B is entered from A reading 0 and from F reading 0, both moving right. So a halt is exactly A>0 1 or F>0 1.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The run structure holds at the switches printed; what the disordered stretch does, and whether it can produce the halting pattern, are open.

check: gcc -O2 -o tmrun tools/c/tmrun.c && ./tmrun 1RB0LD_0RC---_0LD0RF_1LE1LD_0LA0RD_0RB1RA 1000000000 records 100000 > rec.txt && python3 holdouts/1RB0LD_0RC---_0LD0RF_1LE1LD_0LA0RD_0RB1RA/py/shape.py rec.txt c=1100,b=100 && python3 holdouts/1RB0LD_0RC---_0LD0RF_1LE1LD_0LA0RD_0RB1RA/py/switches.py rec.txt c=1100,b=100

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The head shuttles between the ends, rewriting runs of 100 / 1100 into one run of 1100 and back; a trip costs about the width squared, for a few cells of growth, so the width grows like the cube root of the time.

facts.text: Width of the tape at its last extension before step 10<sup>9</sup>.
Side switches in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps.

sections.heading: Runs of words rewritten end to end
html: The tape at the last side switches:

The two runs at the left (409 + 308, then 398 + 319) add up to the one run at the right (716, then 717), to within one word. The left end and the right end carry short disordered stretches; everything else is runs of a single word.

1RB0LD_0RC---_0LD0RF_1LE1LD_0LA0RD_0RB1RA and 1RB0LF_1LC0RD_1LA1LC_---0RE_0RB1RA_1LC1LF behave alike: all 1,423 side switches in the first 109 steps fall on the same sides in both, the widths at the n-th switch differ by at most 1, and the run lengths printed agree (409 and 308, 398 and 319, 716, 717).

sections.heading: Why the width grows like t<sup>1/3</sup>
html: The head goes back and forth across the whole tape. After step 5·108 there are 298 side switches (extensions of the tape on the other side from the last one), on average 1,676,606 steps apart, which is about 0.196·w2 for the final width w = 2924; each adds about 2.0 cells to the width. A constant gain per w2 steps gives w3 ~ t. The fitted exponent of the width after step 107 is 0.326.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.324). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.328).
After 109 steps the tape spans 2,925 cells (1,793 left of the start, 591 right), with a density of 1s of 0.496.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: runs of 1100 rewritten end to end
summary: Two long runs of the word 100 / 1100 at the left end turn into one run of 1100 at the right end, with about as many words, next to a short disordered stretch; the head shuttles between the ends and the width grows like t^(1/3).
